title: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease and Tubo-Ovarian Abscess: Assessment and Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Non-pregnant women with suspected pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), including tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA), in the emergency department (ED), gynaecology or primary care: who to admit, outpatient and inpatient antibiotic regimens including beta-lactam allergy, 72-hour review and follow-up. Uses UCSF infectious diseases guidance based on the CDC 2021 sexually transmitted infection (STI) guidelines, a 2022 American Family Physician summary of those guidelines, and product information. Pregnancy is excluded from the drug regimens because doxycycline is contraindicated.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi PID guideline was found; the full CDC 2021 guideline was not opened (UCSF and American Family Physician summaries were used).
CDC minimum diagnostic criteria were not available in the opened sources; diagnosis relies on clinical judgment and the differential.
TOA drainage thresholds were not given by the opened sources.
Pregnant women with PID need specialist obstetric and infectious diseases advice; no regimen is listed for them.
Partner notification and treatment follow local sexual health services.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: PID is ascending infection of the upper genital tract; treatment covers gonorrhoea, chlamydia and anaerobes (Am Fam Physician 2022, Table 1). Metronidazole is now added to all intramuscular and oral regimens (Am Fam Physician 2022, Table 1). TOA is a complication that needs hospital care (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).

symptoms: Lower abdominal or pelvic pain (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
Fever and vomiting in severe PID (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
physicalSigns: High fever and overt peritonitis in severe PID (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
Adnexal mass suggesting TOA (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
redFlags: Surgical emergency such as appendicitis not excluded: admit (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
Severe PID with vomiting, severe pain, high fever or peritonitis: admit (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
TOA: admit (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
Pregnancy: admit (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
No improvement within 72 hours of outpatient therapy: switch to parenteral therapy and re-evaluate (UCSF PID guidance, Section Follow-up).
precipitants: Sexually transmitted infection with gonorrhoea or chlamydia (Am Fam Physician 2022, Table 1).
Untreated partners (UCSF PID guidance, Section Follow-up).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Cannot be excluded clinically: admit for assessment (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
Positive pregnancy test; PID in pregnancy needs admission (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).

clinicalManagement.title: Assess and decide setting
actions: Pregnancy test, STI swabs, and assessment for surgical emergency, severity and TOA (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).
Admit if any hospitalisation criterion is met (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).

clinicalManagement.title: Outpatient treatment
actions: Ceftriaxone intramuscular once plus doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days (see Medicines) (UCSF PID guidance, Section Outpatient regimen).
Review within 72 hours (UCSF PID guidance, Section Follow-up).

clinicalManagement.title: Inpatient treatment
actions: Cefoxitin intravenously plus doxycycline; after 24 hours of improvement stop cefoxitin, continue doxycycline and add metronidazole (see Medicines) (UCSF PID guidance, Section Inpatient regimen).
Beta-lactam allergy: clindamycin plus gentamicin, then oral doxycycline and metronidazole after 24 hours of improvement (UCSF PID guidance, Section Beta-lactam allergy).
TOA not responding: gynaecology for drainage (UCSF PID guidance, Section Hospitalisation criteria).

clinicalManagement.title: Follow-up and partners
actions: Arrange partner notification and treatment and retest at 3 months through sexual health services (UCSF PID guidance, Section Follow-up).

regimens.indication: PID: single-dose cover for Neisseria gonorrhoeae
regimens.dose: 500 mg intramuscularly once for weight over 45 kg and under 150 kg; 1 g if 150 kg or more (UCSF PID guidance, Section Outpatient regimen).
adjustments: No adjustment in renal or hepatic impairment alone; with both, do not exceed 2 g daily (Ceftriaxone label, Section Dosage and Administration).
If lidocaine is used as diluent for intramuscular injection, observe lidocaine contraindications; never give that solution intravenously (Ceftriaxone label, Section Contraindications).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Observe for allergic reaction after injection (Ceftriaxone label, Section Contraindications).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ceftriaxone or any cephalosporin; higher risk after severe penicillin reactions (Ceftriaxone label, Section Contraindications).

regimens.dose: 2 g intravenously every 6 hours; stop after 24 hours of clinical improvement (UCSF PID guidance, Section Inpatient regimen).
adjustments: Creatinine clearance 30 to 50 mL/min: 1 to 2 g every 8 to 12 hours; 10 to 29: every 12 to 24 hours; 5 to 9: 0.5 to 1 g every 12 to 24 hours; below 5: 0.5 to 1 g every 24 to 48 hours (Cefoxitin label, Section 2.3).

monitoring: Diarrhoea: consider Clostridioides difficile (Cefoxitin label, Section 5.2).
Glucose in diabetes with dextrose-containing product (Cefoxitin label, Section 5.6).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cefoxitin or other beta-lactams (Cefoxitin label, Section 4.1).
Hypersensitivity to corn products for the dextrose formulation (Cefoxitin label, Section 4.2).

regimens.indication: Inpatient PID or TOA with beta-lactam allergy
regimens.patientGroup: Non-pregnant women admitted with PID and beta-lactam allergy
regimens.dose: 900 mg intravenously every 8 hours (UCSF PID guidance, Section Beta-lactam allergy); dilute to 18 mg/mL or less and infuse no faster than 30 mg per minute (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.2).
regimens.duration: Until 24 hours of clinical improvement, then oral doxycycline and metronidazole to complete 14 days
adjustments: Prolonged therapy: check liver and kidney function (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.2).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Diarrhoea: consider Clostridioides difficile colitis, during or weeks after treatment (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.4).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to clindamycin or lincomycin (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.3).
Never as undiluted intravenous bolus (Clindamycin SmPC, Section 4.2).

regimens.indication: Inpatient PID or TOA with beta-lactam allergy
regimens.patientGroup: Non-pregnant women admitted with PID and beta-lactam allergy
regimens.dose: 2 mg/kg intravenously once, then 1.5 mg/kg every 8 hours (UCSF PID guidance, Section Beta-lactam allergy).
regimens.frequency: Every 8 hours after the loading dose
adjustments: Renal impairment: reduce the daily dose and adjust interval to creatinine clearance (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.2).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Levels: 1-hour peak not above 10 mg/L; trough not above 2 mg/L with multiple daily dosing (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.2).
Renal, hearing and balance function (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.4).
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.3).
Hypersensitivity to gentamicin (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.3).
Pregnancy: only if essential (Gentamicin SmPC, Section 4.4).

patientEducation: Take all tablets for the full 14 days even if you feel better.
Partners need testing and treatment; avoid sex until both are treated.
lifestyleAndDiet: Use condoms to reduce future infections.
mdtReferrals: Emergency physician; gynaecologist; infectious diseases or sexual health service; interventional radiology for TOA drainage.
dischargeCriteria: Improving at 72 hours, tolerating oral regimen, pregnancy excluded, partner treatment arranged, follow-up booked.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review within 72 hours, sexual health follow-up with partner treatment and retesting at 3 months (UCSF PID guidance, Section Follow-up).
